proposals.name: Applied technical or professional expertise
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 how much the comment demonstrates the commenter applying specialized knowledge (scientific, engineering, occupational, legal-technical) to explain a mechanism relevant to the rule, rather than voicing a general lay opinion. A 10: the comment explains a specific technical/professional mechanism (e.g., species habitat-use biology, an engineering or clinical process) that only someone with hands-on expertise could produce, and uses it to analyze the rule. A 0: the comment shows no specialized understanding and reads as something any member of the public could write about the topic in general terms.
proposals.rationale: R01 (herpetologist explaining brumation habitat, population fragmentation, and citing specific field discoveries) and R11 (attorney explaining the mine-ventilation mechanics of 'downwind bolting') show dense-favored comments doing real technical work a scorecard keyed to surface features may not register; R46 (no expertise, pure venting) is scorecard-appropriately low and shows the contrast.

proposals.name: Verifiable, source-attributed factual claims
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 how many of the comment's key factual claims are tied to a specific, identifiable, checkable source (named study/author/year, dataset, agency report, or statute) versus claims that float free of any attribution. A 10: nearly every substantive factual claim names where it comes from. A 0: the comment makes factual or statistical assertions but never identifies their source.
proposals.rationale: R01 cites 'Woods et al. 2018' and 'Bergamini et al. 2017' by name for specific population claims, and R07 cites 'FAA data 2003-2017' with an exact rate (0.035%); contrast R04, which asserts a specific demographic statistic (93 million people, 28%) with no source at all, and R28, which asserts a policy conclusion with zero evidentiary support -- a distinction a scorecard built on topical keyword bins may not capture.

proposals.name: Specific, precise proposed regulatory fix
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 how concretely the comment specifies what should change: exact replacement text, a specific numeric threshold, or a precise procedural modification, versus a general expression of support or opposition. A 10: the comment proposes exact substitute wording, a specific number, or an unambiguous procedural change the agency could adopt directly. A 0: the comment states only a general 'for' or 'against' position with no specific alternative.
proposals.rationale: R47 (Cerus) proposes exact replacement sentences for specific guidance passages, and R57 proposes changing a compensation cap from 25% to 100% of pre-fire value; contrast R28 and R46, both of which register a demand or a complaint but no concrete alternative provision -- yet R28 scores very high on the scorecard side, suggesting the scorecard may be rewarding intensity of demand rather than precision of the ask.

proposals.name: Pinpoint engagement with the rule's actual text
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 the degree to which the comment quotes or precisely cites specific provisions (section/paragraph numbers, page numbers, statutory citations) of the proposal and responds to that exact language, rather than discussing the topic in the abstract. A 10: the comment repeatedly quotes or cites specific textual provisions and responds directly to their wording. A 0: the comment never references any specific provision; it could have been written without reading the text.
proposals.rationale: R01 quotes specific page numbers (p. 23625, p. 23608) from the proposed rule, and R45 walks through the exact statutory clause at 16 U.S.C. Sec. 3371(f); contrast R10 and R46, which discuss the general policy area (Medicaid, hangar rules) with no textual anchor anywhere in the comment.

proposals.name: Causal-mechanism reasoning linking rule to effect
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 whether the comment explains WHY the challenged provision will produce its claimed effect through an identifiable step-by-step mechanism, versus simply asserting that an effect will occur. A 10: the comment traces a clear causal chain grounded in how the regulated activity actually works. A 0: the comment states a conclusion with no chain of reasoning connecting the rule to the claimed effect.
proposals.rationale: R11 traces a precise mechanism (ventilation direction reversal -> dust/methane pushed toward bolt crew -> lethal exposure) and R34 traces radium's 1,630-year half-life to multigenerational contamination risk; contrast R28, which asserts administrators 'must go above and beyond' with no mechanism at all connecting any action to any outcome.

proposals.name: Acknowledgment of tradeoffs and counterarguments
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 whether the comment engages with costs, competing interests, or plausible reasons the agency might favor the opposite position, versus being purely one-sided. A 10: the comment explicitly identifies and weighs a genuine tradeoff or counter-consideration even while disagreeing. A 0: the comment shows no awareness that any opposing consideration exists.
proposals.rationale: R01 opens by praising FWS's 'impressive' documentation before critiquing scope, and R25 acknowledges the ACI program's original environmental purpose while flagging the permitting obstacle it created in practice; contrast R10 and R28, which are entirely one-sided with no engagement of any competing interest.

proposals.name: Rule-specific reasoning vs generic sloganeering
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 whether the comment's argument is built from facts and reasoning specific to this particular rule, versus a generic talking point that could be dropped into comments on many different rules essentially unchanged. A 10: the argument's logic clearly required engaging this rule's specific mechanics and could not be reused unmodified elsewhere. A 0: the argument is a generic slogan with no rule-specific development.
proposals.rationale: R13 and R20 are near-identical templated letters (same '$4 to $5 billion' and '37% to 47%' figures, same paragraph structure) submitted by different people, suggesting a coordinated talking point rather than independent analysis of this specific docket; contrast R11 or R23, whose arguments are so specific to the provision at hand (downwind bolting sequencing; OBOGS oxygen-tube contamination thresholds) that they could not be reused verbatim on a different rule.

proposals.name: Epistemic calibration: hedging vs overclaiming
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 whether the comment matches its asserted confidence to the actual strength of its support -- hedging genuinely uncertain or speculative claims, and reserving confident language for well-supported claims. A 10: the comment flags inference, uncertainty, or open questions where appropriate and is confident only where warranted. A 0: the comment asserts speculative or contested claims with total, unqualified certainty.
proposals.rationale: R01 explicitly separates her own research-based judgment from her employer's position, and R60 explicitly flags a gap ('I could not find a study that would refer to the Salton Sea's ability for gas absorption') rather than filling it with assertion; contrast R10, which states contested predictions ('will destroy Medicaid... government-controlled healthcare') as flat certainty with no support, and R02, which declares a contested scientific conclusion settled while citing a study result it also flags as an outlier.

proposals.name: Concrete first-hand observational grounding
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 whether the comment includes specific, checkable first-hand detail -- a named place, date, operational detail, or personally observed event -- that goes beyond what anyone could infer just from reading the proposal. A 10: the comment is anchored in vivid, specific, first-hand operational detail. A 0: the comment is entirely generic, with nothing distinguishing it from something written with no direct experience of the regulated activity.
proposals.rationale: R25 describes the Town of Greeneville's actual air curtain incinerator and the specific TDEC opacity-permit inspections that followed, and R55 names the vessel (Aubrey Joy), home port (New London, CT), and specific fishery it operates in; contrast R33 or R46, which offer only generic sentiment with no first-hand operational anchor.

proposals.name: Downstream or systemic consequence-tracing
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 whether the comment identifies non-obvious secondary, downstream, or systemic consequences (administrability, precedent, ripple effects) beyond the single most immediate and obvious effect of the rule. A 10: the comment traces at least one non-obvious downstream or systemic consequence with explicit reasoning. A 0: the comment addresses only the single most surface-level, immediately obvious effect.
proposals.rationale: R43 (Texas RioGrande Legal Aid) traces vague FEMA rules to downstream harms of unreviewable disparate treatment across disaster-affected communities and to opportunities for fraud, and R42 draws a precedent-based argument by pointing to a parallel CMS decision to demand comparable stakeholder process; contrast R33, which stays at the single-layer level of 'give me access to boosters' with no systemic follow-through.

proposals.name: Coherence between stated rationale and request
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 whether the reasons offered map proportionately and logically onto the specific action requested, versus the rationale and request being disconnected or disproportionate. A 10: every reason given clearly and proportionately supports the specific ask. A 0: the stated rationale bears little logical relationship to the request, or the comment veers into rhetoric unconnected to the rule's technical substance.
proposals.rationale: R51 pivots from a narrow carrot-grading classification change to 'the perfect representation of a democracy... makes me proud to be an American,' rhetoric wildly disproportionate to and disconnected from the technical substance of the grading standard; contrast R45 or R47, where the stated legal/technical rationale and the specific requested textual fix track each other tightly throughout.

proposals.name: Technical and factual precision
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 whether technical, scientific, legal, or economic terms and concepts are used correctly and consistently, versus being conflated or used in ways suggesting a basic misunderstanding of the subject matter. A 10: all technical/factual claims are precise, internally consistent, and correctly deployed. A 0: the comment's use of technical or factual concepts is confused or self-contradictory in ways that undercut its claims.
proposals.rationale: R23 (Boeing) precisely specifies why TCE vapor degreasing must remove contaminants to ppb-level thresholds for oxygen-enriched systems, and R30 correctly and precisely cites specific regulatory facts (FDA-approved for food/drug use, not OSHA-hazardous, insoluble in water) in support of its safety claim; contrast R27, which muddles a cultivar-naming question with an unsupported health-safety inference about walnut color with no basis given.

proposals.name: Responsiveness to what the rule changes
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 whether the comment addresses the specific delta the rule introduces relative to current practice, versus discussing the general subject-matter area without engaging what is actually changing. A 10: the comment precisely identifies and responds to the specific change(s) being proposed. A 0: the comment discusses the general policy area in terms that would apply regardless of what the specific rule change actually is.
proposals.rationale: R05 (BIO) answers each of FDA's four numbered burden questions about the specific proposed information collection, and R38 (TTAG) engages the exact managed-care provisions with specific statutory cross-references (Sec. 1932(a)(2)(C), ARRA Sec. 5006); contrast R33 and R41, which offer general policy sentiment about the broader topic area without pinning down what the specific proposal actually changes.

proposals.name: Feasibility-aware constructive alternative
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 whether the comment offers a path forward that accounts for the agency's likely practical constraints (cost, timing, administrability), versus only stating a problem or demand with no attention to what the agency could feasibly do. A 10: the comment proposes a compromise or phased approach explicitly designed to be workable given the agency's evident constraints. A 0: the comment only opposes, complains, or demands, with no attention to feasibility.
proposals.rationale: R47 (Cerus) offers alternative regulatory language designed to balance blood-safety goals with operational practicality, and R18 (City Utilities) supports EPA's proposed postponement as a workable interim step that respects the ongoing reconsideration process; contrast R46 and R28, which register pure demands/complaints with no feasibility-aware alternative offered.

proposals.name: Reasoning-based persuasion vs rhetorical amplification
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 whether the comment's persuasive force comes from developed reasoning and evidence, versus relying on repetition, capitalization, insults, or hyperbole in place of an argument. A 10: persuasive force rests entirely on developed reasoning/evidence delivered in a measured tone, even when the position is strongly held. A 0: the comment relies on capitalized/repeated demands, insults, or hyperbolic rhetoric as a substitute for developing any argument.
proposals.rationale: R28 consists almost entirely of a capitalized, repeated demand ('DO NOT LISTEN TO POLITICIANS SPOUTING...') with no developed argument, yet it is the single highest card_pct value in the whole slice (0.900), while dense rates it only mid-range (0.467); R46 similarly substitutes insults ('dipshitidiots') for substance. Contrast R01 and R11, whose strongly-held disagreement is carried entirely by developed, measured-tone reasoning rather than rhetorical intensity -- this pairing suggests the scorecard may be rewarding rhetorical amplification that dense discounts.

proposals.name: Provision-level remedy: names the text and the replacement
proposals.instruction: Score how far the comment converts its position into something a drafter could act on. 10 = it identifies the specific provision, paragraph, threshold, table entry, tariff code, or definition at issue AND states what it should say instead (a number to change, a category to delete, a phrase to substitute, a standard to adopt). 5 = it names a specific requirement but leaves the fix implicit ('this should be reconsidered', 'we have concerns'). 0 = it expresses only a direction of preference ('do more', 'protect us', 'act quickly') with nothing operable behind it. Score the operability of the ask itself; a two-sentence comment that says 'change 25 percent to 100 percent in paragraph (c)(2)' scores high, and an elaborate letter that never states a requested change scores low.
proposals.rationale: R32 rewrites paragraph (c)(2) from a 25 percent cap to 100 percent of loss and adds specific compensable items (Habitat Equivalency Analysis, GIS mapping, expert testimony). R60 asks precisely that HTSUS subheading 3301.29.51.50 be removed from Phase VI. R03, despite degraded handwriting and OCR, issues six operable directives (apply the 2016 IRIS Unit Risk Value, delete the startup/shutdown/malfunction exception, require monitoring). All three are dense-high/card-low. R28 and R24, card-high, exhort at length and leave nothing to draft.

proposals.name: Names a specific omission in the agency's supporting analysis
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment engages the agency's own record rather than only its own position. 10 = it points to a particular thing the notice, preamble, or impact analysis failed to address - an unexamined failure mode, an uncosted burden, a population or entity class not analyzed, a required analysis not performed, a study that does not exist - and says why that omission bears on the decision. 5 = it gestures at inadequate analysis without locating the gap. 0 = the agency's record never enters; the comment argues only for its preferred outcome.
proposals.rationale: R15 states that the supplementary information never acknowledges the risk of an unmarked carcass leaving the facility, and asks what oversight covers establishments that never held a waiver. R21 argues the notice fails to account for small entities and should therefore have triggered a regulatory flexibility analysis. R39 reports being unable to find any study of the Salton Sea's gas absorption and asks for localized analysis. All three sit dense-high/card-low, while card-high R35 and R59 never touch the agency's analysis at all.

proposals.name: Shows the proposal departs from the agency's own precedent
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment holds the agency to its own prior behavior. 10 = it identifies what this agency previously did, said, or committed to - a prior demonstration or pilot, a parallel rulemaking, published guidance, a stated regulatory pathway - and shows the current proposal departs from it without explanation, quoting or specifically citing the prior action. 5 = it invokes agency practice in general terms. 0 = no reference to agency conduct outside the instant proposal.
proposals.rationale: R16 reconstructs how the 1999 PPS model was actually built (88 recruited agencies, interviews, OASIS training, in-home logs, additional assessment data) to show HHGM rests on claims data alone, then quotes CMS's own August 2017 cancellation of the EPM and CR models back at the agency. R09 argues FDA has stated numerous times that substantial equivalence, not PMTA, is the pathway for premium cigars, making the proposed cigar standards inconsistent with the agency's own position. Both are dense-high/card-low; a criterion bank scoring the comment in isolation cannot see the agency's prior conduct.

proposals.name: Traceable causal chain from the rule to the claimed effect
proposals.instruction: Score whether consequences are connected to the rule by a mechanism a reader can follow and check. 10 = intermediate steps are named, so the claim is falsifiable (the rule permits A, which changes B, which produces C, which matters because D). 5 = one link is stated and the rest assumed. 0 = consequences are asserted as bare outcomes with no pathway ('this will destroy the program', 'this will endanger everyone'). Judge the presence and checkability of the chain, not whether you agree with its conclusion.
proposals.rationale: R02 runs the chain explicitly: nonnative tilapia and mosquitofish compete for aquatic invertebrates, depleting the turtle's food base, so the designated 12.28 acres must exclude them; then water provisioning sustains vegetation, which sustains invertebrates and provides cover. R37 reasons from chitosan's water-insolubility to low leaching and from microbial enzymatic breakdown to low persistence, and lands on the 'minimum risk' standard the EPA must apply. R34 traces cabin pressure above the threshold to lowered blood oxygen to reduced flow through heart, lungs and brain, to hypoxia. Against these, card-high R27 asserts longer waits and higher death rates with no chain, and R28 asserts an obligation with none.

proposals.name: Field observation that disconfirms a factual premise of the rule
proposals.instruction: Score whether firsthand experience is aimed at a premise rather than at a preference. 10 = the commenter reports something they have directly observed, operated, or measured that contradicts a specific factual assumption the agency is relying on (a stock estimate, an occupancy map, an achievability assumption, an exposure estimate), and identifies which assumption it contradicts. 5 = genuinely relevant firsthand experience offered as grounds for a preference, without confronting any stated premise. 0 = no firsthand observation, or observation with no bearing on any premise.
proposals.rationale: R31 reports that after constraints on NFMA monkfish effort were removed the fleet still could not reach the TAL, and turns that directly against the stock assessment ('it is possible that the stock assessment is wrong'). R58, from twenty-plus years on the species, reports populations found in 2016 and 2019 after the 2013 proposal, contradicting the occupancy snapshot the revised designation rests on. Both are dense-high/card-low. Compare card-high R17 and R18, where real operating experience is offered as grounds for a preference rather than aimed at an assumption.

proposals.name: Tests whether the chosen instrument will actually bind
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment interrogates the mechanism, not just the policy direction. 10 = it asks or shows whether the instrument will change behavior at all - whether a numeric limit sits above observed practice, whether a threshold will ever be triggered, whether the voluntary approach has already been tried and failed, whether the model or measurement underneath the standard can resolve the effect being regulated - and supports the answer. 5 = it questions stringency without examining whether the instrument operates. 0 = it argues only that the policy should be stronger or weaker.
proposals.rationale: R44 observes that historical grouper trips land under 200 lbs, so a 200-lb commercial limit may never bind, and asks for the trip-average data needed to set one that would. R11 notes that only four carriers ever adopted voluntary family-seating policies, which is the evidence that the voluntary instrument failed. R03 attacks AERMOD's known near-field and far-field errors, i.e., the measurement instrument beneath the standard rather than the standard's level. All three are dense-high/card-low.

proposals.name: Splits support and opposition along a stated principle
proposals.instruction: Score internal differentiation. 10 = the comment endorses identifiable parts of the proposal and opposes others, and the dividing line follows from a principle it states (which effects the record supports, which it does not; where flexibility is warranted and where it is not). 5 = mixed reactions expressed without any organizing rationale. 0 = uniform endorsement or uniform rejection with no differentiation. A comment that concedes a real point against its own interest and explains why it still objects scores at the top.
proposals.rationale: R31 supports the SFMA mesh-size change as consistent with traditional practice while opposing the NFMA limit elimination. R15 agrees the added flexibility and its economic benefits are needed, then presses the failure mode the notice ignores. R44 agrees Red Grouper need protection while arguing the rebuilding plan is too weak, provision by provision. R58 opens by commending the quality of the supporting documentation and then dismantles the definition it supports. All four are dense-high/card-low, which suggests a criterion bank reads a differentiated comment as a hedged or weaker one.

proposals.name: Anticipates second-order and precedential effects
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment sees past the rule's face. 10 = it identifies what the change sets in motion beyond its literal terms - the precedent it establishes for future actions, the category or door it opens, parties downstream who absorb the consequence, the incentive it creates - and explains the transmission. 5 = a second-order effect is named without a route. 0 = effects are treated as confined to the rule's literal terms and the commenter's own position.
proposals.rationale: R21 argues that permitting introductions outside historic range would create an unlimited ability to place species anywhere and would broaden the geography of protections even while formally expanding nothing. R15 traces a single unmarked-carcass incident to public scorn absorbed by animal producers far upstream of the establishment that caused it. R42 argues the varietal-exemption removal converts a marketing order into an entry barrier and subverts the purpose of the regulatory framework. R60 shows a catch-all 'other' subheading sweeps in material outside the statutory definition. All four are dense-high/card-low.

proposals.name: Stake declared, then argued in the statute's public terms
proposals.instruction: Composite. Score both parts. 10 = the comment discloses its interest AND translates its ask into the criterion the agency must actually apply (technical feasibility, statutory purpose, risk, evidentiary sufficiency), and where relevant documents the effort it has already made to comply or substitute. 5 = interest disclosed but the entire argument is the commenter's revenue, convenience, or market position. 0 = the ask is naked private advantage, or the stake is concealed while the argument pretends to public grounds.
proposals.rationale: R12 states Boeing's interest, then documents years of qualifying aqueous alternatives, names the applications where none exists (OBOGS oxygen tubes needing ppb-level cleanliness, with fire and explosion consequences), and asks for a bounded exemption rather than defeat of the rule. R42 recasts a commercial objection as misuse of AMS authority by a competing domestic committee. Both dense-high/card-low. Against these, card-high R13 and R29 are the same argument filed from two states resting entirely on the filer's revenue share, and R17 rests on lost bookings; the scorecard appears to credit the presence of impact reasoning without asking whose criterion it speaks to.

proposals.name: The analysis is the commenter's own, not incorporated or reproduced
proposals.instruction: Score whose reasoning is doing the work. 10 = the substantive analysis is developed by the submitter and applied to this docket; outside sources appear as support for the commenter's own argument. 5 = the commenter's own analysis is present but thin, leaning on a summary of another filer's position. 3 = the comment is a wrapper around block-quoted or incorporated-by-reference material that carries all of the substance, so the agency learns nothing it would not learn from the underlying filing. 0 = the comment reproduces another author's text with a signature attached and adds no reasoning of its own. Score provenance of reasoning, not the presence of quotations or citations, which can be entirely legitimate.
proposals.rationale: R04 wraps two sentences of its own around a long verbatim statement by a third-party watchdog chairman. R07 states 'broad support' for AASHTO's comments and a five-state joint filing and says it will 'briefly reiterate' them. R22 explicitly refers back to and reiterates the recommendations of a 2015 letter. All three are card-high/dense-low. A bank that scores propositions cannot see that the propositions were authored elsewhere; R16 and R58, card-low, build arguments that exist nowhere else in the docket.

proposals.name: Information yield: tells the agency something it did not have
proposals.instruction: Score the density of decision-relevant information the agency plausibly lacked. 10 = a reader comes away with facts, constraints, mechanisms, or consequences new to the record. 5 = accurate and relevant but already known to the agency. 0 = the comment occupies the shape of a response - taking each solicited question in turn - while answering with nothing ('reasonable', 'not unusual nor burdensome', 'we cannot comment', 'we support any and all means'). Deduct for the absence of information, never for the presence of background or context; the question is what remains after the framing is removed.
proposals.rationale: R35 answers all four Paperwork Reduction Act questions and conveys essentially nothing: the burden estimate is 'reasonable', the policy requirement is 'not unusual nor burdensome', and on utility it 'cannot comment'. R59 similarly ends at the point where substance would start. Both are card-high, which is what a bank rewarding responsiveness-to-solicited-questions would do. R03 and R58, card-low, are dense in facts per line - six technical directives with numeric bases, and a stream of population records with page-level engagement with the notice.

proposals.name: Identifies a conflict with operative statutory text
proposals.instruction: Score legal grounding by whether a conflict is demonstrated. 10 = the comment quotes or precisely cites the controlling provision and shows the proposal cannot be squared with it, or that it triggers a procedure the statute requires and the notice omitted. 5 = a relevant statute or standard is cited but the tension is asserted rather than shown. 0 = no legal grounding, or citations used as decoration. Score the demonstrated conflict, not the number or formatting of citations.
proposals.rationale: R60 sets the catch-all 'other essential oils' subheading against the Lacey Act's definition of 'plant' at 16 U.S.C. 3371(f) and asks for its removal on that ground. R09 argues Congress barred FDA from banning tobacco products in the 2009 Act, so a de facto ban via the PMTA pathway exceeds authority. R21 argues the change triggers a regulatory flexibility analysis that the notice never performed. All three are dense-high/card-low. Note that strong versions also appear on the card-high side (R38 on 30 U.S.C. 863(b), R50 on National Standards 2 and 4), which is exactly why the criterion must score the conflict rather than the citation density.

proposals.name: Workable alternative with feasibility and transition reasoning
proposals.instruction: Score the constructiveness of the ask. 10 = the comment offers a specific alternative, accommodation, or scope carve-out AND addresses what makes it workable - cost, timing, who administers it, what has already been tried and failed, an existing program it can be modeled on. 5 = an alternative is named with no feasibility reasoning. 0 = no alternative is offered; the comment only blocks or only endorses.
proposals.rationale: R12 asks for a bounded ten-year aerospace exemption and justifies it with the failure of aqueous substitution for named parts and the inadequacy of the 18-month and 2-year transition windows. R30 proposes booster access for all age groups on a six-month interval, administered on the model of the annual flu vaccine. R41 asks that the proposed Category 3 telehealth policy be extended to hospital outpatient departments by parity of reasoning with physician practices. R02 proposes water provisioning to carry the designated habitat through drought. All four are dense-high/card-low.

proposals.name: Engages the alternatives the agency considered and the decision at hand
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment argues against the agency's actual framing. 10 = it addresses the option the agency declined, the rationale the agency offered for its choice, or the scope line the agency drew, and argues against that reasoning on its own terms. 5 = it argues for a different outcome without engaging the agency's stated reasoning. 0 = it argues past the proposal entirely - restating a general policy preference, or attacking a decision that is not before the agency in this docket.
proposals.rationale: R44 targets the plan's specific decision not to add May to the offseason and argues from the February-June spawning window. R32 engages FEMA's stated reason for the 25 percent cap - consistency with the Cerro Grande process - and the New Mexico tort baseline the agency invoked, before rejecting both. R58 engages the exclusion of unoccupied areas at the specific pages of the notice that draw the line. On the other side, card-high R57 answers a request for information about publishing testing data with a broadside that random testing is 'fundamentally misguided', and card-high R04 opposes phosphate mining generally when the question is road construction use.

proposals.name: Confidence proportionate to evidence; strongest counter-consideration met
proposals.instruction: Score the fit between what is claimed and what is offered. 10 = claims are stated at the strength the support carries, uncertainty is marked where it exists, and the most serious consideration cutting the other way is named and answered. 5 = claims somewhat outrun their support, or the opposing interest is acknowledged only formally. 0 = maximal claims with no support, or the countervailing interest never appears. Judge the assertion-to-support fit; do not score politeness, vocabulary, or intensity by themselves - a blunt comment whose claims are backed scores high, and a courteous one whose claims are not scores low.
proposals.rationale: R34 states the comparison explicitly - the potential health risks outweigh the economic benefits to the airline industry - after laying out the exposure evidence and thresholds. R15 concedes the flexibility and economic benefit are warranted before pressing its concern, and frames the residual as questions rather than conclusions. R37 walks the hazard and environmental-fate evidence before concluding the minimum-risk standard is met. All three are dense-high/card-low. Against them, card-high R27 asserts crashed systems, longer waits and higher death rates with no support and no countervailing consideration, and R28 escalates into capitals around a single unsupported demand.

proposals.name: Pinpointed Textual Correction
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies precise proposed language or a defined provision and supplies a concrete replacement or revision; score 0 when it offers only a general view without locating the regulatory text at issue.
proposals.rationale: This distinguishes actionable regulatory analysis from broad positions in R15 and R18, while R04 and R30 mainly state opposition and preferred outcomes.

proposals.name: Explicit Causal Mechanism
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment clearly explains the step-by-step mechanism connecting the proposal to a specific benefit, harm, or behavioral response; score 0 when it merely asserts that consequences will occur.
proposals.rationale: R46 traces how an unmarked carcass could create downstream public-health and reputational risks, and R48 connects habitat conditions, prey, predators, drought, and turtle survival. R45 mostly asserts sweeping consequences without a developed mechanism.

proposals.name: Traceable Evidence Use
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when claims are supported by identifiable studies, datasets, statutes, official analyses, or clearly described observations whose relevance and limitations are explained; score 0 when claims are unsupported or rely on vague references.
proposals.rationale: R32 names peer-reviewed studies and contrasts them with the assessment used, while R42 cites specific population discoveries and research. R28 and R57 make serious claims without traceable supporting evidence.

proposals.name: Quantitative Magnitude And Context
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment uses relevant numbers, denominators, comparisons, or calculations to show the scale and practical significance of an effect; score 0 when numbers are absent, unexplained, or merely rhetorical.
proposals.rationale: R23 provides a 15-year positive-test rate and relates it to testing costs, while R55 discusses mileage, capacity, connectivity, and affected industries. R26 describes safety concerns without quantifying their prevalence or magnitude.

proposals.name: Uncertainty And Counterargument
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment acknowledges plausible uncertainty or opposing considerations, evaluates them, and explains why its recommendation remains preferable; score 0 when it treats its own position as self-evident and ignores contrary evidence.
proposals.rationale: R25 distinguishes SOFR from LIBOR through two specific risks and examines substitution concerns, while R39 questions the reliability of favorable stock assessments. R19 and R34 rely almost entirely on certainty and indignation.

proposals.name: Alternative And Tradeoff Analysis
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment compares the proposal with one or more feasible alternatives and explicitly weighs their different benefits, costs, risks, or enforcement effects; score 0 when it demands adoption or withdrawal without comparison.
proposals.rationale: R04 contrasts prohibition with education, cessation support, prevention, and regulated alternatives, while R47 distinguishes viable from technically infeasible substitute processes. R35 rejects a use without seriously comparing workable disposal alternatives.

proposals.name: Operational Feasibility
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment explains how affected parties would actually implement, administer, document, or comply with the proposed approach and identifies concrete operational obstacles; score 0 when implementation is discussed only abstractly.
proposals.rationale: R03 describes municipal disposal operations and opacity-compliance problems, while R51 explains reporting workflows, controls, unresolved data questions, and timing. R17 praises flexibility without describing implementation.

proposals.name: Edge-Case Safeguards
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies a foreseeable exceptional case or failure mode and proposes a targeted safeguard, exception, threshold, or contingency; score 0 when it assumes ordinary conditions and offers no protection against foreseeable failures.
proposals.rationale: R46 asks how oversight would address establishments without updated controls, and R18 addresses shortages, interstate shipments, low yields, and licensing boundaries. R54 supports the rule without testing its treatment of difficult cases.

proposals.name: Law Applied To Facts
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment accurately connects specific statutory or regulatory language to concrete facts and explains why the proposal is authorized, unauthorized, required, or constrained; score 0 when legal references are conclusory or ornamental.
proposals.rationale: R07 applies Mine Act provisions to ventilation-plan approval and downwind bolting, while R29 connects transparency concerns to several statutory requirements. R43 invokes regulatory-flexibility obligations but develops the factual and legal connection only briefly.

proposals.name: Firsthand Observation Translated
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when personal or local experience is translated into a specific, generalizable regulatory observation, mechanism, or data need; score 0 when experience is presented only as emotion or personal preference.
proposals.rationale: R12 connects lived experience in the Coachella Valley to localized monitoring and possible Salton Sea emissions, and R02 connects community exposure to specific monitoring and modeling requests. R09 mainly reports personal and customer hardship without developing a testable regulatory insight.

proposals.name: Distributional Incidence Analysis
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies which distinct groups, locations, firms, or vulnerable populations bear benefits and burdens, and explains why those effects differ; score 0 when it invokes a generic public or industry without analyzing distribution.
proposals.rationale: R56 explains distinct effects on tribal health systems, providers, and American Indian and Alaska Native patients, while R58 identifies chilling effects on immigrant families and citizen children. R30 largely invokes small businesses and communities generically.

proposals.name: Evaluation And Monitoring Design
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment proposes measurable indicators, data collection, study design, review timing, or feedback procedures that would test whether the regulatory approach is working; score 0 when it requests action without specifying how performance or unintended effects should be assessed.
proposals.rationale: R27 criticizes the absence of demonstrations, interviews, logs, and stakeholder testing, while R52 calls for evaluation of campaign effects and dissemination of findings. R20 urges targets but supplies little monitoring design.

proposals.name: System Interaction Analysis
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment shows how the proposal interacts with other rules, institutions, markets, technologies, or sequential decisions and identifies resulting coordination effects; score 0 when it analyzes the proposal in isolation.
proposals.rationale: R60 explains how inconsistent tax classifications could create mismatches across Code sections, and R32 connects federal zones, state representation, stock science, and complementary management. R05 mostly evaluates the guidance question in isolation.

proposals.name: Proportionality And Calibration
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment matches the stringency, scope, timing, or burden of its recommendation to the severity, likelihood, and distribution of the identified risk; score 0 when the recommendation is categorical and uncalibrated.
proposals.rationale: R13 distinguishes a percentage cap from full loss, restoration, expert costs, and cultural harms, while R38 proposes risk-tiered licensing with lighter treatment for low-risk systems. R34 demands rejection without calibrating the asserted burden or risk.

proposals.name: Scope Discipline And Prioritization
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment stays focused on provisions it can substantively assess, ranks its concerns, and clearly separates central recommendations from peripheral or unsupported issues; score 0 when it is diffuse, repetitive, or equally emphatic about unrelated points.
proposals.rationale: R38 limits its analysis to capabilities directly related to its operations and develops a structured risk-tier proposal, while R59 identifies the precise Phase VI elements it addresses and expressly distinguishes silence from agreement. R45 and R19 spread broad claims across the rule without prioritization.

proposals.name: Mechanistic causal chain
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment traces a concrete chain from a proposed provision through implementation to specific effects, with assumptions made explicit; score 0 when it asserts only that the rule is good or harmful.
proposals.rationale: R19 links cabin-pressure thresholds to hypoxia and affected passengers; R50 links unmarked carcasses to oversight gaps and public-health risk.

proposals.name: Corrective specificity
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies precise text, threshold, definition, exemption, boundary, or procedure to change and states the requested replacement; score 0 when the requested action is merely support or opposition.
proposals.rationale: R10 specifies monitoring, risk thresholds, modeling, and startup provisions; R54 proposes multiple exact revisions to pathogen-reduction guidance.

proposals.name: Evidence-to-claim traceability
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when important factual claims are tied to identifiable studies, datasets, statutory materials, or clearly described observations; score 0 when claims are unsupported assertions or slogans.
proposals.rationale: R34 names and characterizes two peer-reviewed population-genetics studies; R43 connects habitat recommendations to named studies and newly documented populations.

proposals.name: Challenge to agency assumptions
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies a specific premise, dataset, model, or inference in the proposal and presents concrete evidence or reasoning that could disprove or materially revise it; score 0 when it merely disagrees with the conclusion.
proposals.rationale: R05 challenges HHGM’s reliance on claims data by contrasting it with missing assessment and stakeholder evidence; R26 questions whether earlier filing dates meaningfully advance the stated fraud-detection purpose.

proposals.name: Implementation realism
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment explains how regulated parties, administrators, systems, personnel, or timelines would operate under the proposal and identifies practical implementation constraints; score 0 when implementation is ignored.
proposals.rationale: R14 discusses referral procedures, screening methods, transfers, and existing security workflows; R36 explains systems, controls, unresolved guidance, and timing problems created by the filing change.

proposals.name: Unintended-consequence safeguards
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies a plausible secondary failure or harm and proposes a concrete safeguard, monitoring step, exception, or contingency; score 0 when it predicts harm without explaining the pathway or mitigation.
proposals.rationale: R50 identifies the risk of an unmarked carcass leaving a facility and asks how oversight would address it; R04 considers health, supply, demand, and grower-investment consequences of expanding walnut categories.

proposals.name: Viable alternative design
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment offers a practicable alternative regulatory design that advances the stated objective while addressing the identified defect; score 0 when it offers no alternative beyond withdrawing or enforcing the proposal.
proposals.rationale: R20 supports localized air-quality analysis and additional source investigation; R24 proposes removing permitting barriers because air-curtain incinerators could replace open burning.

proposals.name: Legal and authority reasoning
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment accurately connects its recommendation to quoted or clearly identified statutory requirements, delegated authority, legal standards, or limits; score 0 when legal language is invoked only rhetorically.
proposals.rationale: R38 interprets specific Mine Act provisions to require lowest-attainable dust exposure; R28 uses Lacey Act definitions to argue that a tariff category exceeds statutory scope.

proposals.name: Distributional incidence
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment distinguishes effects across affected populations, locations, firm types, or vulnerable groups and explains why those differences matter; score 0 when it discusses only the writer’s undifferentiated interest.
proposals.rationale: R40 details distinct effects on tribes, Indian health providers, managed-care organizations, and patients; R19 distinguishes risks to infants, adults with health conditions, and travelers at high-elevation airports.

proposals.name: Dynamic and time-horizon reasoning
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment analyzes how effects change over time, including adaptation, delayed harms, stock or market dynamics, transition periods, or intergenerational consequences; score 0 when it treats impacts as immediate and static.
proposals.rationale: R09 emphasizes respiratory disease that may emerge decades after exposure; R15 connects spawning seasons, rebuilding periods, historical catch levels, and ecosystem recovery.

proposals.name: Operational domain knowledge
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when specialized experience is translated into generalizable facts about how the regulated activity actually works and why the rule interacts with it; score 0 when identity or claimed experience is offered without operational insight.
proposals.rationale: R14 explains cargo-screening layers and referral practices from the pilot; R39 identifies technically constrained aerospace cleaning applications and the contamination levels required for safe oxygen systems.

proposals.name: Uncertainty calibration
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment distinguishes established facts, estimates, hypotheses, and unknowns, states material uncertainty, and makes recommendations conditional where appropriate; score 0 when confidence is absolute despite missing or contested information.
proposals.rationale: R07 separates the structural differences between SOFR and LIBOR and notes the unresolved spread issue; R57 questions a favorable stock assessment while describing the evidence and uncertainty behind that concern.

proposals.name: Measurement and evaluation design
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment specifies what should be measured, compared, monitored, or studied, including useful metrics or comparison groups; score 0 when it calls for more research or transparency without saying what information would resolve the issue.
proposals.rationale: R27 requests evaluation of campaign effects on knowledge, attitudes, and behavior and dissemination to target communities; R15 proposes studying actual commercial-trip catches to set a meaningful limit.

proposals.name: Omission detection
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies a material population, condition, data source, activity, or risk omitted from the proposal and explains how that omission changes the analysis; score 0 when it merely lists additional topics without showing their relevance.
proposals.rationale: R10 points to background ethylene-oxide levels, model error, and startup conditions omitted from the risk treatment; R17 identifies cultural, ecological, restoration, and evidentiary losses not captured by the compensation limit.

proposals.name: Objective-burden proportionality
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment weighs the rule’s stated objective against quantified or concretely described burdens and recommends a proportionate scope, timing, threshold, or exemption; score 0 when it treats either the objective or the burden as dispositive without comparison.
proposals.rationale: R39 supports replacing TCE where feasible but requests targeted relief for technically irreplaceable aerospace uses; R01 explains why transition guidance must preserve economic terms while preventing collateral tax consequences.

proposals.name: Campaign mail-merge signature block (name + city, state)
proposals.instruction: Score how strongly the comment's closing matches a mass-campaign mail-merge format: a plain personal name immediately followed by 'City, ST ZIP' with no title, organization, or contact info, appended to a short, generically-applicable body. 10 = textbook mail-merge signature (bare name + city/state/zip closing a generic, could-apply-anywhere body). 5 = a personal name+location sign-off but the body contains some docket-specific content. 0 = no personal name+city signature block at all (unsigned, or institutional letterhead signature with title/organization instead).
proposals.rationale: R28 ('Sincerely, Lynn Ryan, Torrance, CA 90505') and R30/R57 (near-duplicate food-additive letters closing 'Thank you, Jenny Cordova, Corrales, NM' / 'Ellen Ingber, Millburn, NJ') all show this exact signature convention; R30 and R57 are otherwise near-verbatim, proving the personalization is cosmetic. This mail-merge personalization can make a comment read as an authentic individual voice to a dense reader even though the substance is identical across many signers.
proposals.upstream_parent: the comment was generated by an organized advocacy campaign's mail-merge/action-alert tool that appends each individual signer's name and city to a shared template

proposals.name: Formal institutional filing apparatus / letterhead conventions
proposals.instruction: Score the density of formal legal/regulatory filing conventions: an addressee block, a 'Re:' case caption with docket/RIN number, numbered footnotes describing the association's membership or assets, a formal salutation ('Dear Sir or Madam'), and a closing with a professional title. 10 = full law-firm/trade-association filing apparatus present (address block + Re: caption + footnoted membership stats + titled signature block). 0 = plain conversational text with no address block, no formal salutation, and no filing conventions.
proposals.rationale: R06 (Hogan Lovells law firm letterhead, docket caption, internal file number), R39 (German Banking Industry Committee, numbered footnotes on membership), R46 (Institute of International Bankers, addressee block to named Treasury/IRS officials), and R47 (American Bankers Association, formal 'Re:' caption and footnoted trillion-dollar figures) all carry this apparatus; a well-resourced organization's professional drafting staff could also produce genuinely more rigorous legal argument, so the fingerprint is confounded with real expertise.
proposals.upstream_parent: the comment was drafted by professional legal counsel, in-house regulatory/tax staff, or a paid lobbyist following standard formal rulemaking-filing conventions

proposals.name: Docket number cited as decorative legitimacy header
proposals.instruction: Score whether a precise docket/RIN/case number is cited prominently (e.g., in a 'Re:' line or parenthetical) while the surrounding paragraphs never quote, paraphrase, or specifically analyze the language of that cited document or provision. 10 = docket number(s) cited precisely and prominently, but the argument that follows is generic talking points not tied to any specific language in the cited notice. 0 = no docket number is cited, or a cited docket number is followed by direct quotation/analysis of that specific text.
proposals.rationale: R07 ('Re: Docket Numbers EPA-R08-OAR-2023-0489-0001 and EPAR08OAR20240389') and R48 ('Re: Docket Number EPAR08OAR20240389'), both from the same haze-rule campaign family, cite exact docket numbers up front but the body never quotes or parses the actual State Implementation Plan text -- it recites the same generic SCR/cost-effectiveness talking points regardless of the specific docket.
proposals.upstream_parent: campaign organizers or professional drafters pre-fill official docket metadata into an otherwise generic-content template to lend it apparent procedural legitimacy

proposals.name: OCR/scan artifact noise in submitted text
proposals.instruction: Score visible evidence that the text passed through OCR or was retyped from a scanned/faxed document: broken word spacing (e.g., 'Postpouemeut', 'Compliauce'), header/footer fragments interleaved mid-paragraph, stray page numbers, or garbled characters. 10 = heavy, frequent OCR-type garbling running throughout the text. 0 = clean, apparently born-digital text with no such artifacts.
proposals.rationale: R12 ('Postpouemeut of Certaiu Compliauce Dates', 'Submitted Electrouical/y') and R18 ('Mischelaneous', 'UAR 2 3 2020', 'V A OOCKET CENTER') both show heavy OCR-style garbling; R34 ('mothod', 'aud') and R32 (raw email-header fragments 'Perez, JuanB / From: / Sent: / To: / Subject:') show milder versions -- none of this noise reflects the argument's substance, only its digitization pathway.
proposals.upstream_parent: the comment was originally filed on paper, by fax, or as a scanned PDF and entered the docket via OCR rather than as born-digital text, indicating an older or less digitally-native submission channel

proposals.name: Emotional-hook opening sentence before substantive content
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment opens with a short, punchy, emotionally-loaded sentence or fragment functioning as a headline/attention-grabber (a declarative claim of personal harm, moral outrage, or a rhetorical jab) before any substantive policy content appears. 10 = a clear stand-alone emotional hook line opens the comment, disconnected from any immediately following factual support. 0 = the comment opens directly with a substantive claim, fact, or procedural statement, with no rhetorical hook.
proposals.rationale: R07 opens with 'You and your loved ones breathe the same air they destroy' before any policy content, and R19 opens with 'This rule has got to be one of the dumbest rules to come out of the dipshitidiots running the FAA' -- both are attention-grabbing headline sentences that carry emotional charge but no evidentiary content on their own.
proposals.upstream_parent: surface-only

proposals.name: Rhetorical-question barrage without corresponding assertions
proposals.instruction: Score the extent to which the comment substitutes a string of open-ended questions addressed to the agency for declarative claims or evidence. 10 = the comment's persuasive content is carried primarily by a series of unanswered rhetorical questions. 0 = the comment makes declarative assertions supported by reasons or evidence, with at most an incidental rhetorical question.
proposals.rationale: R14 (walnut coloring: 'does that mean that all variations of red are okay to eat then?', 'how were they being sold before?') and R31 (HHGM: 'Will CMS please share the demonstration...', 'Are we... to understand...') and R56 (carcass marking: 'What possible risk of such happening will incur...', 'what oversight will the FSIS have...') are all built around unanswered questions rather than asserted positions; a judge could reward the appearance of critical engagement here even though no claim is actually substantiated, though sincere questioning can also reflect genuine independent scrutiny.
proposals.upstream_parent: the submitter lacks specialized domain briefing and is thinking through the rule in real time rather than being coached by domain experts or a campaign talking-points sheet

proposals.name: Generic template / form-letter phrasing likelihood
proposals.instruction: Score how likely the paragraph content is to be a reused, mass-produced template rather than text specifically composed for this docket: generic statements that would apply equally to almost any similar proceeding, canned statistics or phrases that read as pre-scripted talking points, and an absence of any detail specific to this particular notice or its facts. 10 = entirely generic/interchangeable content with canned statistics that could be dropped unchanged into many different dockets on the same broad topic. 0 = content is clearly specific to this docket's particular facts, provisions, or circumstances and could not be reused elsewhere unchanged.
proposals.rationale: R01 and R11 are near-identical letters ('flavored cigars alone generate $4 to $5 billion in annual retail sales and make up 37% to 47%...') differing only in the submitter's state (Illinois vs. Florida); R30 and R57 are likewise near-identical food-additive letters differing only in signer name/city. Both pairs demonstrate that the substantive paragraphs are canned and interchangeable across submitters.
proposals.upstream_parent: the paragraph is reused near-verbatim from a mass-distributed advocacy or industry campaign template, i.e. it is part of a coordinated campaign

proposals.name: Deferential praise-laden tone toward the agency
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment includes explicit praise, gratitude, or expressions of trust directed at the agency or its staff (e.g., thanking them for their dedication, calling the process something that makes the submitter proud, opening with unprompted thanks). 10 = comment contains clear unprompted praise or gratitude toward the agency's competence, effort, or process. 0 = comment is neutral or openly adversarial/accusatory toward the agency, with no praise language.
proposals.rationale: R52 opens 'First, thanks to the Department of Transportation for balancing the timely promulgation...' and urges the agency to 'stay its course,' and R22 closes 'Thank you for your dedication and drive to improve our carrot grading system for the better... makes me proud to be an American' -- both pair praise/gratitude with support for the rule, a tone that is separate from whether the underlying argument is well-reasoned, though genuine repeat stakeholders who have this rapport may also bring real substantive familiarity.
proposals.upstream_parent: the submitter has, or is seeking, an ongoing cooperative relationship with the agency (a repeat industry commenter, or a lay commenter unusually deferential to authority) rather than being an adversarial outside critic

proposals.name: Bare unsourced numeric statistics used for rhetorical weight
proposals.instruction: Score the presence of precise-sounding numeric claims (dollar figures, percentages, counts) stated as fact without any citation, footnote, or named source. 10 = comment leans on multiple precise unsourced statistics presented as established fact. 0 = no numeric claims are made, or all numeric claims are explicitly attributed to a named or cited source.
proposals.rationale: R01 and R11 both assert 'flavored cigars alone generate $4 to $5 billion in annual retail sales and make up 37% to 47% of popular price large cigars sold' with no citation or source named, and R49 asserts 'we've saved more than $46 billion as of this moment!' with no source -- in all three cases a precise-sounding number is used to manufacture an impression of factual grounding without any way for a reader to verify it.
proposals.upstream_parent: surface-only

proposals.name: Coalition / membership-breadth enumeration as legitimacy signal
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment explicitly enumerates or quantifies the breadth of the submitter's coalition or membership (naming member companies, partner states/agencies, or stating a specific membership/assets figure) as a way of establishing standing, independent of the substantive argument. 10 = comment prominently lists member organizations/partner states or cites a specific large membership or assets number as a legitimacy marker. 0 = comment speaks only in the voice of the individual submitter with no membership/coalition breadth claims.
proposals.rationale: R34 (Montana DOT: 'MDT and our rural western state partners (Wyoming, Idaho, North Dakota and South Dakota) filed joint comments'), R35 (Express Association of America / Cargo Airline Association listing DHL, FedEx, UPS, ABX Air, Atlas Air, Kalitta as members), and R44 (Autonomous Vehicle Industry Association listing 18 named member companies and '44 million autonomous miles') all use explicit coalition/membership enumeration as a standing signal; larger coalitions may also field more substantive expertise, so the signal is genuinely confounded with real resources.
proposals.upstream_parent: the submitter belongs to a well-resourced trade association or coalition with dedicated government-affairs staff whose standard practice is to assert scale and breadth for negotiating leverage

proposals.name: Outside-counsel production marks: DMS stamps, file codes, transmittal lines
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for how strongly the text carries the production residue of a professional legal or regulatory-affairs document pipeline, ignoring what the comment argues. Award points for: a document-management-system footer or version stamp (e.g. a bare alphanumeric string like 'DC - 703150/000300 - 8664524 v2' or '106085429.v1-12/16/19' sitting alone on a line); internal file or reference codes ('Ref. DK: USQ', 'Ref. BdB: ST.20.02', 'Prepared by Ls/Nf'); a formal transmittal line in caps ('VIA ELECTRONIC SUBMISSION', 'By Electronic Delivery', 'Submitted through the Federal eRulemaking Portal'); running per-page headers that repeat docket number, date and 'Page N of M'; the honorific 'Esq.' or a named firm. A 10 has three or more of these marks. A 0 is text with none of them - no footers, no file codes, no transmittal line, no page furniture.
proposals.rationale: These marks are pure artifacts of the drafting shop's software and workflow; they contain zero argument. But they co-occur with a whole register the dense model reads end-to-end. R35 (Hogan Lovells) carries a bare DMS stamp mid-document and a repeated docket/page header; R04 (Cigar Rights of America) carries the version-stamp line '106085429.v1-12/16/19' plus 'VIA ELECTRONIC SUBMISSION'; R08 (German Banking Industry Committee) carries 'Ref. DK: USQ' and 'Prepared by Ls/Nf'; R13 signs 'Sam B. Petsonk, Esq.'. Marked mixed because paid counsel plausibly also produces better-evidenced comments - the channel cannot be reported as pure noise, only as a resource fingerprint whose sign must be measured separately from merit.
proposals.upstream_parent: the comment was drafted and produced by outside counsel or a standing professional regulatory-affairs function, rather than typed by the submitter

proposals.name: Mail-merge campaign residue: trailing docket line, name-city-ZIP signoff
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 for evidence that the text was emitted by a mass-campaign submission platform rather than composed and filed by the signer. Award points for: a signature block of bare name, city, two-letter state and a nine-digit ZIP appended after the argument; the docket or 'Re:' line appearing at the END of the comment, after the argument, rather than at the top; residual mail headers from a campaign vendor (From:/To:/Date:/Subject: lines, or an address at a bulk-mail domain); bulleted asks rendered with an odd platform delimiter (e.g. '::' or '*' repeated as list markers); an argument body that reads as a fixed template with one or two slots filled. A 10 shows the trailing docket block or vendor headers plus the name-city-ZIP tail. A 0 is a comment whose docket reference (if any) is at the top and which carries no appended address, no vendor headers, and no template slotting.
proposals.rationale: Placement of a 'Re: Docket Number' block AFTER the argument is a mechanical artifact of a platform appending the routing line to a fixed body - it says nothing about the argument. R29 and R59 both bury 'Re: Docket Number EPA-R08-OAR...' at the very bottom after the substantive text and both sit in the dense-high half (dense .447 / .542) against card .039 / .109. R12 and R16 are the same body with only the signer's name and city swapped, both with the '::' bullet delimiter and a nine-digit ZIP tail; R42 repeats the shape; R54 still carries the vendor's own header block (an @everyactioncustom.com sender, a To: A-AND-R-DOCKET line, a stray '376.txt' filename). The card model is near-blind to all of these (card .036-.144) while dense is not, so the residue is exactly the kind of thing dense is reading. Not mixed: a campaign platform does not make the underlying argument better.
proposals.upstream_parent: submission routed through a coordinated advocacy campaign platform, so the comment's shape is set by the vendor rather than the signer

proposals.name: Quantified membership and economic-footprint self-credentialing
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on how much of the comment is spent quantifying the submitting organisation's own size, reach or economic weight - member counts, asset totals, employee counts, market share, covered-lives figures, miles or shipments - as distinct from evidence about the rule. A 10 devotes a full paragraph or a long footnote to figures like 'over 1,600 banks', 'more than 2,300 companies', 'US banking assets over 3.7 trillion dollars', 'coverage for 105 million Americans', '44 million autonomous miles', 'more than 65,000 pilots'. A 5 gives a one-line institutional identification with a single number. A 0 makes no quantified claim about the submitter at all, either because the submitter is an individual or because the letter goes straight to the merits.
proposals.rationale: The footprint paragraph is a status display aimed at the reader, not evidence about the rule, and it is boilerplate reused across every docket the organisation files in. It saturates one side of the slice: R25 (Institute of International Bankers, 35 countries, 3.7 trillion dollars, 15 of 24 primary dealers), R37 (American Bankers Association, 16 trillion dollar industry, 2 million employees), R45 (Mortgage Bankers Association, 280,000 people, 2,300 companies), R50 (Blue Cross Blue Shield, 105 million Americans), R08 (1,600 German banks, 90 percent of the certificate market) - dense .162 to .372 for all of them. R22 (Autonomous Vehicle Industry Association, 44 million miles, 'roughly equivalent to 184 trips to the moon') shows the same display at dense .824, so the sign is not obvious and must be measured. Mixed is true: an organisation with those resources plausibly also writes better-evidenced comments.
proposals.upstream_parent: the submitter is a resourced trade association or large firm with a standing government-affairs function whose house style is to establish weight before arguing

proposals.name: Administrative-mechanics subject register versus embodied-consequence register
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on where the comment's substance sits between two poles, judging only the KIND of thing at stake, never how well it is argued. Score 10 when the entire substance is procedural or classificatory machinery: filing deadlines and extensions, paperwork and information-collection burden estimates, form series, tax sourcing and characterisation rules, licensing tiers, definitional taxonomy, which subheading a product falls under. Score 0 when the substance turns on embodied consequence to people, animals or places: deaths, disease, injury, explosion or fire, extinction, habitat loss, contaminated water, lost livelihoods. Score 5 for economic-impact-only arguments with no bodies and no machinery. Do not reward or penalise argument quality, citation density, or length.
proposals.rationale: This is a property of the rule, not of the comment: an outstanding comment about a thirty-day filing extension is still an outstanding comment. The split is stark. Pure machinery: R37 (elimination of automatic 30-day extensions for information returns, dense .247), R39 (classification of cloud transactions under sections 1.861-18 and -19, dense .046), R50 (Form 1095 filing deadline, dense .372), R07 (whether a Paperwork Reduction Act burden estimate is reasonable, dense .344), R49 (a three-tier licensing taxonomy, dense .149). Embodied consequence: R22 (42,795 road deaths, 7,508 pedestrian deaths, dense .824), R38 (students carrying inhalers, asthma admissions, dense .838), R60 (contaminants causing fire or explosion in an oxygen-enriched system, dense .728), R03 (extinction risk to two gartersnake species, dense .889). Mixed is true because salient, high-stakes dockets also attract the most capable commenters.
proposals.upstream_parent: which docket the comment landed in - the agency and the genre of the rule - which determines both who shows up and how the whole comment reads, independent of any property of this submitter

proposals.name: Front-matter latency before the first substantive claim
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 by how much apparatus the reader must pass before the comment's first substantive assertion about the rule. Count everything that is not argument: an attachment stub ('See attached file(s)', 'Please see the attached'), letterhead spill (street address, suite, PO box, telephone, fax, web URL, tagline), the date line, one or more addressee blocks, a multi-line RE: reproducing the full title of the rule, salutation, and an institutional identification paragraph. Score 10 when roughly a page of such apparatus precedes the first claim, or when the rule's full title is reproduced across many lines before anything is asserted. Score 0 when the first sentence of the document already makes a claim about the rule. Judge position only; do NOT score total length - a short comment can score 10 and a very long one 0.
proposals.rationale: Latency is a property of the production pipeline, not of the reasoning, and it is separable from length, which is already declared. The low-latency end of the slice is also its dense-high end: R11 opens mid-argument in its first clause (dense .969, the highest here), R32 asserts in sentence one (dense .835), R09 and R55 likewise (dense .557, .575). The high-latency end runs the other way: R25 spends an address block, mission statement, date and two addressee blocks before its first claim (dense .234); R50 stacks date, addressee, RE, salutation and a federation-description paragraph (dense .372); R15 reproduces the docket title twice in broken OCR columns before arguing (dense .555); R56 and R10 have the same shape (dense .323, .306). Mixed is true - an organisation with a letterhead workflow is also an organisation with staff.
proposals.upstream_parent: the submitter produced a letterhead PDF through an organisational document workflow and attached it, rather than typing into the web comment box

proposals.name: Unglossed sector shorthand and program-insider acronym density
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on how far the comment presumes the reader is a colleague inside the same program. Award points for domain acronyms and program names used without expansion on first use, for informal references to internal instruments (plans, waivers, assessments, seasons, panels) as if both parties already track them, and for shop-floor phrasing about how the program actually operates day to day. A 10 is unreadable to an educated outsider without a glossary - e.g. HACCP plans, Sanitation SOPs and prerequisite programs thrown out unexplained, or DAS, SFMA, NFMA and TAL used bare, or HHGM, PPS, OASIS, CJR and EPM stacked in consecutive sentences. A 0 spells out every term or writes in plain language throughout. Score only the shorthand, not whether the underlying point is correct.
proposals.rationale: Unexplained shorthand is a membership signal, not an argument: the same point written out longhand for a lay reader would be equally meritorious and would score 0 here. The three individual comments in this slice with the densest insider shorthand are also three of its highest dense scores - R11 (HACCP plans, Sanitation SOPs, prerequisite programs, waivers; dense .969), R47 (HHGM, PPS, OASIS, CJR, EPM, CMS-5524-P; dense .854), R40 (monkfish DAS, SFMA, NFMA, TAL, stock assessment; dense .781) - while the card model rates all three near the floor (.036 to .310). Counter-cases exist (R51 uses ACL, SEDAR28 and ASMFC at dense .365), so the sign must be measured. Mixed is true because genuine sector embeddedness plausibly also produces better-informed comments.
proposals.upstream_parent: the submitter's seniority and embeddedness in the regulated sector - a practitioner who deals with this program office routinely writes to it the way they talk at work

proposals.name: Accusatory stance toward the agency or a rival interest
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on how adversarial the comment's posture is, independent of whether the accusation is supported. Score 10 for explicit imputation of bad faith, illegality, capture or contempt - accusing the agency of violating its own statute or an oath, calling the rule or its authors names, or alleging that a competitor or advisory committee is bending the regulatory process to raise barriers against the commenter. Score 5 for firm disagreement framed as error or oversight ('the agency erred', 'the analysis fails to account for'). Score 0 for a uniformly cooperative posture that frames every disagreement as a request for clarification or a suggested revision. Judge posture only, not evidence.
proposals.rationale: Posture is a rhetorical choice available at any level of evidence, so it cannot itself be merit: in this slice R36 accuses the California Desert Grape Administrative Committee of using AMS and USDA regulatory power to create barriers to entry and offers no evidence at all (dense .792), while R34 is equally accusatory about FEMA and is heavily statute-cited (dense .103) - accusation and evidence come apart cleanly. The accusatory end skews dense-high here: R36 (.792), R47 (rhetorical challenges to CMS, .854), R31 ('purely political purposes', .756), R09 (open contempt for the FAA, .557) against cooperative letters like R07 (.344) and R02 (line-edit requests only, .330). Not marked mixed precisely because the slice shows the parent producing both well- and poorly-evidenced comments.
proposals.upstream_parent: whether the submitter has an ongoing working relationship with this agency that they need to protect - regulated entities with a standing relationship hedge, outsiders and one-off filers do not

proposals.name: Unsolicited commendation of agency staff and process
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on how much the comment praises the agency itself - its staff, its effort, its priorities, or the rulemaking process - beyond the pro-forma 'we appreciate the opportunity to comment' line, which does not count. Score 10 for explicit commendation of the work or the workers ('kudos to the staff who undertook such a massive job', 'Service staff are to be commended', 'thanks to the Department for balancing the mandate with industry concerns', 'thank you for your dedication and drive', 'Great initiative'). Score 5 for a single warm sentence about the proposal being a step in the right direction. Score 0 for no praise of the agency anywhere. Do not count praise of the underlying policy goal by third parties, and do not count the ritual opening thanks.
proposals.rationale: Praise of the drafters is addressed to the reader's ego and carries no information about the rule, so it cannot be merit; but it is a distinctive, cheap-to-detect register marker. It concentrates in the dense-high half: R03 ('kudos to the US Fish and Wildlife Service staff', 'to be commended for that effort', dense .889), R32 ('Thank you for your dedication and drive to improve our carrot grading system', dense .835), R01 ('thanks to the Department of Transportation for balancing', dense .598). The card model is near-blind to it in exactly these rows (.463, .394, .164). Honest counter-case: R44 ends 'Great initiative.' at dense .201, so the channel is not deterministic. Not mixed - the disposition to flatter is not a cause of better evidence.
proposals.upstream_parent: coaching from an advocacy group or a naive model of how the process works - the submitter believes goodwill is currency here, which tracks submitter type rather than argument strength

proposals.name: Personal-standing wrapper carrying borrowed industry-wide statistics
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on the mismatch between the comment's claimed personal standing and the provenance of its evidence. Score 10 when the comment opens by asserting a specific personal role and locale ('As a small-business operator in Florida', 'As a resident of X') and then argues entirely from national aggregate figures, market-share percentages and sector talking points that no individual in that role would have at hand, with no observation specific to the writer's own operation. Score 0 when the claimed standing is actually used to deliver first-hand observation that only that person could supply - what they personally saw, measured, or did over what period. Score 5 when personal observation and borrowed aggregates are genuinely balanced. Ignore whether the aggregates are correct.
proposals.rationale: This isolates astroturf from genuine lay expertise, which the length- and citation-based surface tells cannot separate, and it is the sharpest split in the slice. R27 and R58 are the same letter with only the state swapped ('As a small-business operator in Florida' / 'in Illinois'), each pivoting immediately to '4 to 5 billion in annual retail sales' and '37 to 47 percent of popular price large cigars' - figures no single retailer holds - and both sit at the very bottom of the dense range (dense .055 and .058) while the card model is fooled (card .609, .611). The opposite pole is dense-high: R38 uses its resident standing to report students carrying inhalers and what he heard volunteering at Eisenhower Medical Center (dense .838), and R03 argues from 'my own 20+ years of research with Thamnophis rufipunctatus' (dense .889). Not mixed - the template's origin is not a cause of first-hand knowledge.
proposals.upstream_parent: a trade association or campaign supplied a template to nominal members, so a personal voice is wrapped around centrally drafted advocacy material
