proposals.name: Third-party block-quotation dependence
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on what fraction of the comment is verbatim material lifted from a source other than the writer - a named third party's public statement, the rule preamble, a statute or regulation quoted at length, or an agency document reproduced in blocks. Score 10 when more than half the words are quotation and the writer's own contribution is an introduction and a closing line (for example, a short lead-in followed by many paragraphs attributed to a named outside advocate). Score 5 when quotation is roughly a quarter of the text. Score 0 when there is no block quotation and every sentence is the writer's own. Count length of quoted material, not whether quoting was appropriate.
proposals.rationale: Quotation share is measurable from text alone and is a fingerprint of where the content came from, not of how good it is. R19 is the extreme: a short personal opening, then roughly seventy percent of the comment is explicitly attributed to Glenn Compton of ManaSota-88, and it sits at dense .051 against card .500 - the card model scores the borrowed content, the dense model apparently does not. R33 recites the current public-charge definition verbatim at length (dense .242) and R13 quotes 30 U.S.C. 863(b) and (o) in blocks (dense .350), both in the dense-low half, while the quotation-free R11 and R32 are dense .969 and .835. Marked mixed honestly: extensive statutory quotation is also what a competent legal comment does, so the parent plausibly touches genuine quality as well.
proposals.upstream_parent: reliance on an intermediary's prepared material - a watchdog group's talking points, counsel's statutory excerpts - rather than the submitter's own analysis, i.e. a coordination or delegation fingerprint

proposals.name: OCR and portal residue
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the text contains conspicuous extraction or ingestion artifacts—stray page numbers, broken words, malformed spacing, email-routing debris, or corrupted headers—and 0 when it is cleanly rendered prose.
proposals.rationale: R11, R29, R30, and R31 contain conspicuous OCR, email, spacing, and malformed-word artifacts that could cue a model independently of substance.
proposals.upstream_parent: Scanned-document conversion and docket-ingestion workflow

proposals.name: Coordinated copy-paste language
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when distinctive sentences, paragraph order, statistics, and calls to action are duplicated or nearly duplicated across comments, and 0 when the wording is clearly independently composed.
proposals.rationale: R35 and R55 are effectively identical, while R28 and R57 repeat the same flavored-cigar template; campaign duplication is predictive of provenance, not independent merit.
proposals.upstream_parent: Mass advocacy campaign or coordinated comment drive

proposals.name: Litigation-brief posture
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment adopts an adversarial legal-brief structure with claims of statutory conflict, plain-text mandates, legal jeopardy, formal violations, and requested legal remedies; score 0 when it lacks that posture.
proposals.rationale: R10 frames the rule as legally jeopardizing miners and argues statutory compulsion, while R39 repeatedly alleges violations of National Standards and demands emergency legal action; counsel involvement may also improve legal substance.
proposals.upstream_parent: Professional litigation or regulatory-counsel involvement

proposals.name: Quantified institutional scale
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the commenter foregrounds multiple figures proving organizational scale—members, employees, assets, customers, market share, or operational miles—and 0 when no institutional scale is asserted.
proposals.rationale: R06 emphasizes $3.7 trillion in assets and market-loan shares, R12 emphasizes 65,000 pilots, and R25 emphasizes 44 million autonomous miles; these prestige cues can influence model scores apart from the argument.
proposals.upstream_parent: Organisational resources and perceived sector standing

proposals.name: Docket-lineage familiarity
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment narrates prior filings, earlier amendments, pilot participation, waivers, agency precedents, or repeated involvement in the same regulatory process; score 0 when it treats the docket as entirely new.
proposals.rationale: R08 cites earlier AASHTO, coalition, and 2016 submissions; R16 invokes CMS’s prior model practices; and R59 identifies the commenters as original ACAS co-creators after a seven-year pilot.
proposals.upstream_parent: Existing agency relationship and incumbent participation in the docket

proposals.name: Agency-native consultation mapping
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment mirrors the notice’s numbered topics or questions, uses agency-specific section labels, limits itself to requested issues, and offers procedural follow-up; score 0 when it is not mapped to the agency’s consultation structure.
proposals.rationale: R17 answers four FDA information-collection questions explicitly, R36 follows NOAA’s Topic 2 subparagraphs, and R54 answers a numbered FDA hearing question; this process fluency need not equal substantive merit.
proposals.upstream_parent: Regulatory-affairs sophistication and familiarity with agency consultation procedures

proposals.name: Deference sandwich
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment opens with thanks or praise, acknowledges the agency’s goals, and then advances a narrowly framed exception or revision; score 0 when it is uniformly supportive, hostile, or uncalibrated.
proposals.rationale: R03 praises flexibility while raising a focused carcass-marking concern, R06 appreciates Treasury’s effort before isolating one objection, and R25 supports AEB while requesting industry-sensitive implementation; the genre can look thoughtful without proving merit.
proposals.upstream_parent: Professional lobbying and relationship-preserving drafting norms

proposals.name: Embodied local witness voice
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment combines a named occupation, residence, family or community identity, and firsthand observations of local effects; score 0 when it contains no personal or locally situated witness account.
proposals.rationale: R41 identifies an owner-operator and describes customers’ dependence, R45 combines residence with tutoring and hospital experience, and R58 identifies an affected landowner; firsthand experience can be relevant evidence but also acts as a salience cue.
proposals.upstream_parent: Constituent standing and perceived affectedness of the submitter

proposals.name: Accusatory moral urgency
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment uses direct second-person blame, insults, all-caps or emphatic imperatives, catastrophe language, and moral condemnation; score 0 when the register is restrained and technical.
proposals.rationale: R02 uses insults and a direct command to the FAA, R44 accuses agencies of endangering everyone, and R49 uses repeated all-caps imperatives; emotional arousal is not substantive policy quality.
proposals.upstream_parent: surface-only

proposals.name: Attachment-wrapper dependence
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the visible submission is mainly a cover note, letterhead, routing information, or “see attached” notice with little substantive text; score 0 when the comment is fully self-contained in the visible text.
proposals.rationale: R07, R25, R43, R50, and R54 explicitly present formal comments as attached letters, exposing packaging and metadata that may cue the dense model despite the unseen attachment’s contents.
proposals.upstream_parent: Document-packaging and attachment-submission workflow

proposals.name: Organizational scale self-credentialing
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment foregrounds quantified membership, customers, assets, market share, national reach, or institutional prestige; score 0 when it makes no organizational-scale claims.
proposals.rationale: Scale claims may cue attention or deference without proving the specific argument. R10 claims four of five leading manufacturers and 47 member companies; R60 claims members from over 35 countries and $3.7 trillion in U.S. banking assets.
proposals.upstream_parent: submitter resources, status, and perceived agency importance

proposals.name: Access-and-continuity choreography
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment signals an ongoing agency relationship through prior meetings, pilot participation, named officials, offers to discuss issues, or collaborative language; score 0 when it is a one-off submission with no such cues.
proposals.rationale: Relationship-maintenance language can predict perceived consequentiality independently of merit. R11 requests another telephone conference with the agency; R49 calls the commenters original ACAS “co-creators” and emphasizes continued work with CBP and TSA.
proposals.upstream_parent: existing relationships and privileged access to agency personnel

proposals.name: Precedent-chain anchoring
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment densely anchors its position in prior rules, earlier docket filings, agency statements, pilots, amendments, or historical practice; score 0 when it addresses only the current proposal without a regulatory history.
proposals.rationale: Long participation histories can make a commenter appear authoritative even when the current submission adds little merit. R12 reiterates earlier AASHTO and multistate filings; R53 compares the revision with the 2013 proposal and decades of research history.
proposals.upstream_parent: incumbent stakeholder participation and familiarity with the docket lifecycle

proposals.name: Coalition amplification signals
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment speaks for multiple associations or members, endorses allied submissions, names coalition partners, or describes broad sector coverage; score 0 when it presents only an individual, unaffiliated position.
proposals.rationale: Coalition backing may increase perceived weight without making the particular reasoning stronger. R12 invokes AASHTO and several western-state partners; R49 jointly represents EAA and CAA and identifies their major carrier members.
proposals.upstream_parent: coordinated mobilization and organizational capacity

proposals.name: Litigation-ready statutory attack
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment frames the proposal as legally vulnerable, identifies precise statutory commands, argues that the agency lacks discretion, or references litigation; score 0 when it contains no legal-threat or statutory-validity framing.
proposals.rationale: Litigation posture can attract attention as a power signal, while legal aggressiveness is not itself substantive merit. R39 repeatedly says the rule will be in “legal jeopardy” and that MSHA lacks discretion; R55 cites pending lawsuits and alleges statutory violations.
proposals.upstream_parent: lawyer involvement and litigation leverage

proposals.name: Operational implementation microdetail
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment supplies granular workflow, equipment, filing, validation, staffing, transition, or compliance-process details from inside an affected operation; score 0 when it offers only broad policy preferences or values.
proposals.rationale: Operational detail can signal an influential insider even when its policy implications are unsupported. R15 discusses PAS validation, platelet yields, licensing, and interstate shipment exceptions; R51 describes reporting systems, controls, unresolved identifiers, and filing-process changes.
proposals.upstream_parent: submitter proximity to regulated operations and implementation resources

proposals.name: Campaign provenance artifacts
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the text shows coordinated-campaign fingerprints such as duplicated unusual wording, recurring issue order, pasted third-party passages, advocacy-platform metadata, or identical formatting; score 0 when it appears individually authored and bespoke.
proposals.rationale: Campaign provenance may make a comment appear salient through volume or recognizable advocacy language, not merit. R14 and R18 are nearly identical additive-policy submissions; R21 and R35 repeat the same flavored-cigar text with only location and name changes.
proposals.upstream_parent: coordinated advocacy campaign or form-letter mobilization

proposals.name: Authority-borrowing without integration
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment displays statistics, studies, URLs, or agency citations mainly as credibility tokens without explaining methods, uncertainty, or how they establish the requested change; score 0 when it has no such authority display or fully integrates the evidence.
proposals.rationale: Borrowed authority can inflate perceived sophistication without demonstrating relevance or validity. R05 lists named cobia studies and precise catch figures but gives limited methodological integration; R21 cites market-size and youth-use statistics primarily to support a generic economic narrative.
proposals.upstream_parent: professional advocacy drafting and credibility signaling

proposals.name: Submission-production residue
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when visible text contains OCR corruption, duplicated headers, raw email routing, attachment placeholders, odd spacing, extraction errors, or other ingest artifacts; score 0 when the prose is cleanly presented.
proposals.rationale: Production artifacts can become stable model cues while carrying no substantive information. R41 contains severe spacing, OCR, and spelling corruption; R44 contains repeated extraction errors and malformed words; R56 includes raw email metadata and pasted file-processing residue.
proposals.upstream_parent: document-production, scanning, and docket-ingestion pipeline

proposals.name: Personalized grassroots anchoring
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when a broadly framed policy request is anchored in first-person identity, locality, occupation, personal experience, or a localized emotional hook; score 0 when the submission is impersonal and institutionally framed.
proposals.rationale: Personalization can signal mobilized public interest without adding reliable evidence about the proposal. R20 and R43 begin with personal health or local-experience hooks before using highly standardized haze language; R57 combines local anecdotes about the Coachella Valley with a general support message.
proposals.upstream_parent: grassroots constituency activation and personalized form-letter outreach
